summary_en: CELM raised its FY2027 year-end dividend forecast by 1.50 yen to 9.50 yen per share, bringing the full-year dividend to 17.00 yen, up 1.50 yen from the prior forecast and 2.00 yen from the prior fiscal year. The company cited progress in FY2027 results through Q2, disciplined share buyback execution, and sustainable cash flow generation under its progressive dividend policy targeting ROE of 30% or above.
title_en: Notice on Revision of Dividend Forecast (Dividend Increase)
translation_en_brief:
CELM's board of directors voted on November 13, 2026, to raise the year-end dividend forecast for the fiscal year ending March 31, 2027, from 8.00 yen per share to 9.50 yen per share, increasing the full-year dividend prediction from 15.50 yen to 17.00 yen per share. This represents an increase of 1.50 yen from the previous forecast announced on May 14, 2026, and 2.00 yen from the prior fiscal year's actual dividend of 15.00 yen. The second quarterly dividend (paid mid-period) remains undisclosed.

The company completed its share repurchase program in July 2026, acquiring 478,500 shares for 159.6 million yen against an original authorization of up to 550,000 shares and 200 million yen. The underutilized portion of the buyback budget has freed up distributable cash reserves. Additionally, the company reported that cumulative results through the second quarter have tracked solidly against full-year guidance, providing confidence in current business forecasts. CELM is also preparing for the optional adoption of International Financial Reporting Standards in the fiscal year ending March 2028, which prompted management to review sustainable shareholder return levels based on medium to long-term earnings power and cash generation capacity.

CELM operates under a progressive dividend policy that treats the prior year's dividend as a floor, balancing growth investment with shareholder returns while pursuing a target return on equity (ROE) of 30% or above. Management stated that the increase reflects a commitment to fuller profit distribution to shareholders while preserving financial flexibility for growth capital expenditures.
